title: DefenseClaw — AI Discovery Runtime Planes
description: What actually ran, next to AI Discovery's inventory of what is present. Coverage is the first row on purpose: findings from a blinded host must not be read as a clean result.

list.name: host
list.label: Host
list.description: host_name of the records. Narrows every Loki panel; defaults to All.

list.name: user
list.label: User regex
list.description: Regex over user.id (the kernel uid). Narrows the panels whose records carry a user: kernel events, kernel denials, burn-in and agent activity.

list.name: connector
list.label: Connector
list.description: Connector of a kernel denial (enforcement.block.applied, initiator kernel); denials the gateway could not attribute have none and show under All.

panels.title: Coverage — can this host see anything?
Planes not running
panels.description: Selected planes that are not producing observations. Any non-zero value means findings from this host are incomplete. A detector reporting clean because it was never able to look is indistinguishable, on a dashboard, from a host that is genuinely clean — which is why this tile is first.

targets.expr: count(sum by (body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_plane) (count_over_time(({service_name="defenseclaw"} | json | __error__="" | host_name=~"$host" | event_name="ai.runtime.plane_health" | body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_plane_running="false")[5m]))) or vector(0)

panels.title: Processes observed
panels.description: Processes inspected in the latest runtime poll. This remains useful evidence when no process crosses the finding threshold.

targets.expr: max(max_over_time(({service_name="defenseclaw"} | json | __error__="" | host_name=~"$host" | event_name="ai.runtime.plane_health" | unwrap body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_processes_observed)[5m]))

panels.title: Connections observed
panels.description: Network connections inspected in the latest runtime poll, including ordinary traffic that did not produce a finding.

targets.expr: max(max_over_time(({service_name="defenseclaw"} | json | __error__="" | host_name=~"$host" | event_name="ai.runtime.plane_health" | unwrap body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_connections_observed)[5m]))

panels.title: Unattributable connections
panels.description: Outbound connections observed with no owning process. On an unprivileged POSIX host this is how much of the machine's egress cannot be named — the difference between a quiet host and a blind sensor. Windows reports the owning pid in every row, so a non-zero value there means something else.

targets.expr: max(max_over_time(({service_name="defenseclaw"} | json | __error__="" | host_name=~"$host" | event_name="ai.runtime.plane_health" | unwrap body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_connections_unattributed)[5m]))

panels.title: Processes not fully readable
panels.description: Processes this run could see but not fully read. Non-zero is ordinary on an unprivileged run and is a coverage statement rather than an error.

targets.expr: max(max_over_time(({service_name="defenseclaw"} | json | __error__="" | host_name=~"$host" | event_name="ai.runtime.plane_health" | unwrap body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_processes_skipped)[5m]))

panels.title: Partial poll cycles
panels.description: Cycles reported with outcome `partial` rather than `completed`. A degraded poll is never reported as a complete one, so this counts exactly the cycles whose findings must be read as incomplete.

targets.expr: max(count_over_time(({service_name="defenseclaw"} | json | __error__="" | host_name=~"$host" | event_name="ai.runtime.plane_health" | outcome="partial")[5m])) or vector(0)

panels.title: Plane C events classified
panels.description: Kernel observations classified into an AI-agent tactic during the latest Plane C poll. This is useful positive evidence even when no observation becomes a finding.

targets.expr: max(max_over_time(({service_name="defenseclaw"} | json | __error__="" | host_name=~"$host" | event_name="ai.runtime.plane_health" | unwrap body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_host_plane_observations)[5m]))

panels.title: Plane C events gated
panels.description: Kernel observations excluded because they were outside a discovered AI-agent process lineage. This shows how much host noise Plane C filtered without exporting process or payload content.

targets.expr: max(max_over_time(({service_name="defenseclaw"} | json | __error__="" | host_name=~"$host" | event_name="ai.runtime.plane_health" | unwrap body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_host_plane_gated)[5m]))

panels.title: Plane health — every plane, every cycle
panels.description: One record per plane per cycle, emitted whether the plane is up or down. If health were reported only while a plane worked, a dead subscription would leave no trace, and absence is the hardest thing to alert on. `body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_plane_mechanism` names what observes the host on every cycle; `body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_plane_reason` is present only when a plane is down or partly blind, with the remediation.

targets.expr: {service_name="defenseclaw"} | json | __error__="" | host_name=~"$host" | event_name="ai.runtime.plane_health"

defaults.noValue: No plane health samples in range

panels.title: Plane C source — which backend, and what it lost
panels.description: The process backend behind Plane C per host: the DefenseClaw-side `native` sources (cn_proc, fanotify) or the host's own Tetragon read by the root sensor helper. Events lost comes from the backend's own counters and shows `unknown` when they could not be read. Container events were counted and kept out of host agent sessions.

targets.expr: sum by (host_name, backend, mechanism) (count_over_time(({service_name="defenseclaw"} | json | __error__="" | host_name=~"$host" | event_name="ai.runtime.plane_health" | body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_plane="c" | label_format backend="{{.body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_plane_backend}}", mechanism="{{.body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_plane_mechanism}}")[$__range]))

max by (host_name, backend, mechanism) (max_over_time(({service_name="defenseclaw"} | json | __error__="" | host_name=~"$host" | event_name="ai.runtime.plane_health" | body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_plane="c" | body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_loss_known="true" | label_format backend="{{.body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_plane_backend}}", mechanism="{{.body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_plane_mechanism}}" | unwrap body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_events_lost | __error__="")[$__range]))

sum by (host_name, backend, mechanism) (sum_over_time(({service_name="defenseclaw"} | json | __error__="" | host_name=~"$host" | event_name="ai.runtime.plane_health" | body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_plane="c" | label_format backend="{{.body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_plane_backend}}", mechanism="{{.body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_plane_mechanism}}" | unwrap body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_container_events | __error__="")[$__range]))

panels.title: Hosts reporting kernel controls
panels.description: Hosts whose sensor helper reported its kernel controls (plane c plane_health with helper_mode) in the last 10 minutes. Counts each host's current state, from the defenseclaw_kernel_state gauge (one series per host at 1, the state it left at 0), so a host that recovered is no longer counted.

targets.expr: count(max by (host_name) (defenseclaw_kernel_state{host_name=~"$host"}) > 0) or vector(0)

panels.title: Hosts with a stale approval
panels.description: Hosts in enforce whose enforce_ack lists no digest of the build they run (approval stale): every user there is in monitor until the new digest is approved. Alert DefenseClawKernelAckStale. Counts each host's current state, from the defenseclaw_kernel_state gauge (one series per host at 1, the state it left at 0), so a host that recovered is no longer counted.

targets.expr: count(max by (host_name) (defenseclaw_kernel_state{host_name=~"$host", approval="stale"}) > 0) or vector(0)

panels.title: Hosts on fallback
panels.description: Hosts where Tetragon is installed and the helper uses it, but Plane C runs on the native backend (cn_proc and fanotify): no kernel control is enforced there. Alert DefenseClawTetragonFallback. Counts each host's current state, from the defenseclaw_kernel_state gauge (one series per host at 1, the state it left at 0), so a host that recovered is no longer counted.

targets.expr: count(max by (host_name) (defenseclaw_kernel_state{host_name=~"$host", backend="native", tetragon_installed="true", helper_mode!="off"}) > 0) or vector(0)

panels.title: Paused hosts
panels.description: Hosts whose kernel enforcement is paused (tetragon pause): every user on the host is in monitor until it expires or is resumed. Alert DefenseClawKernelPausedLong. Counts each host's current state, from the defenseclaw_kernel_state gauge (one series per host at 1, the state it left at 0), so a host that recovered is no longer counted.

targets.expr: count(max by (host_name) (defenseclaw_kernel_state{host_name=~"$host", paused="true"}) > 0) or vector(0)

panels.title: Kernel denials (every user)
panels.description: Denials of DefenseClaw's kernel controls in range, from the helper's own counter (plane_health blocked_delta), so a denial the gateway could not attribute counts too.

targets.expr: sum(sum_over_time(({service_name="defenseclaw"} | json | __error__="" | host_name=~"$host" | event_name="ai.runtime.plane_health" | body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_plane="c" | unwrap body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_blocked_delta | __error__="")[$__range])) or vector(0)

panels.title: Would-blocks (every user)
panels.description: Accesses a kernel control in monitor mode would have denied, in range, from the helper's own counter (plane_health would_block_delta): each one restarts that user's burn-in.

targets.expr: sum(sum_over_time(({service_name="defenseclaw"} | json | __error__="" | host_name=~"$host" | event_name="ai.runtime.plane_health" | body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_plane="c" | unwrap body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_would_block_delta | __error__="")[$__range])) or vector(0)

panels.title: Kernel controls per host (last 10 minutes)
panels.description: The latest plane c plane_health of each host: the Tetragon version, the Plane C backend, the enterprise.tetragon mode, the approval of this build's controls, how many enrolled users enforce and how many are still in burn-in, the pause, and the control-set digest. A host that changed state in the window shows one row per state. One row per host: its latest record of the last 10 minutes (the state it left is not listed).

targets.expr: max by (host_name, version, backend, mode, approval, paused, digest) (last_over_time(({service_name="defenseclaw"} | json | __error__="" | host_name=~"$host" | event_name="ai.runtime.plane_health" | body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_plane="c" | body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_helper_mode!="" | label_format version="{{.body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_tetragon_version}}", backend="{{.body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_plane_backend}}", mode="{{.body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_helper_mode}}", approval="{{.body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_approval}}", paused="{{.body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_paused}}", digest="{{.body_defenseclaw_policy_version}}" | unwrap body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_users_enrolled | __error__="")[10m])) and on (host_name, version, backend, mode, approval, paused, digest) topk by (host_name) (1, max by (host_name, version, backend, mode, approval, paused, digest) (last_over_time(({service_name="defenseclaw"} | json | __error__="" | host_name=~"$host" | event_name="ai.runtime.plane_health" | body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_plane="c" | body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_helper_mode!="" | label_format version="{{.body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_tetragon_version}}", backend="{{.body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_plane_backend}}", mode="{{.body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_helper_mode}}", approval="{{.body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_approval}}", paused="{{.body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_paused}}", digest="{{.body_defenseclaw_policy_version}}" | label_format ts=`{{ __timestamp__ | unixEpoch }}` | unwrap ts | __error__="")[10m])))

max by (host_name, version, backend, mode, approval, paused, digest) (last_over_time(({service_name="defenseclaw"} | json | __error__="" | host_name=~"$host" | event_name="ai.runtime.plane_health" | body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_plane="c" | body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_helper_mode!="" | label_format version="{{.body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_tetragon_version}}", backend="{{.body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_plane_backend}}", mode="{{.body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_helper_mode}}", approval="{{.body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_approval}}", paused="{{.body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_paused}}", digest="{{.body_defenseclaw_policy_version}}" | unwrap body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_users_enforced | __error__="")[10m])) and on (host_name, version, backend, mode, approval, paused, digest) topk by (host_name) (1, max by (host_name, version, backend, mode, approval, paused, digest) (last_over_time(({service_name="defenseclaw"} | json | __error__="" | host_name=~"$host" | event_name="ai.runtime.plane_health" | body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_plane="c" | body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_helper_mode!="" | label_format version="{{.body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_tetragon_version}}", backend="{{.body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_plane_backend}}", mode="{{.body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_helper_mode}}", approval="{{.body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_approval}}", paused="{{.body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_paused}}", digest="{{.body_defenseclaw_policy_version}}" | label_format ts=`{{ __timestamp__ | unixEpoch }}` | unwrap ts | __error__="")[10m])))

max by (host_name, version, backend, mode, approval, paused, digest) (last_over_time(({service_name="defenseclaw"} | json | __error__="" | host_name=~"$host" | event_name="ai.runtime.plane_health" | body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_plane="c" | body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_helper_mode!="" | label_format version="{{.body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_tetragon_version}}", backend="{{.body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_plane_backend}}", mode="{{.body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_helper_mode}}", approval="{{.body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_approval}}", paused="{{.body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_paused}}", digest="{{.body_defenseclaw_policy_version}}" | unwrap body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_users_burn_in | __error__="")[10m])) and on (host_name, version, backend, mode, approval, paused, digest) topk by (host_name) (1, max by (host_name, version, backend, mode, approval, paused, digest) (last_over_time(({service_name="defenseclaw"} | json | __error__="" | host_name=~"$host" | event_name="ai.runtime.plane_health" | body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_plane="c" | body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_helper_mode!="" | label_format version="{{.body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_tetragon_version}}", backend="{{.body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_plane_backend}}", mode="{{.body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_helper_mode}}", approval="{{.body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_approval}}", paused="{{.body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_paused}}", digest="{{.body_defenseclaw_policy_version}}" | label_format ts=`{{ __timestamp__ | unixEpoch }}` | unwrap ts | __error__="")[10m])))

defaults.noValue: No host reported kernel controls in the last 10 minutes

panels.title: Findings by severity
panels.description: Scored runtime findings over time, banded. No single host-plane tactic reaches high on its own; a high or critical band means several observations combined, or a kill chain progressed.

targets.expr: sum by (body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_severity) (count_over_time(({service_name="defenseclaw"} | json | __error__="" | host_name=~"$host" | event_name="ai.runtime.finding")[$__interval]))

panels.title: Inventory agreement
panels.description: How the discovery inventory answered each finding. `unaccounted` is the interesting reading: a complete scan that explains none of what the runtime planes are watching. `unobserved` means there was no usable inventory and the score was left untouched in both directions.

targets.expr: sum by (body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_correlation_verdict) (count_over_time(({service_name="defenseclaw"} | json | __error__="" | host_name=~"$host" | event_name="ai.runtime.finding")[$__interval]))

panels.title: Runtime findings
panels.description: One record per scored finding. `body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_signals` is the evidence trail behind the score, rendered signal_id=weight. `body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_cmdline` and `..._providers` are content-class fields, so whether they appear here depends on the redaction profile this destination selected.

targets.expr: {service_name="defenseclaw"} | json | __error__="" | host_name=~"$host" | event_name="ai.runtime.finding"

panels.title: Host plane — what an agent did to the machine
Tactics by stage
panels.description: Observed host-plane tactics, in kill-chain order. Every one is gated on an AI agent appearing in the process lineage: a developer running sudo produces nothing here, the same sudo under an agent produces a signal. Renders empty unless the host plane is enabled, which is worth knowing before reading an empty row as a clean host.

targets.expr: sum by (body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_tactic) (count_over_time(({service_name="defenseclaw"} | json | __error__="" | host_name=~"$host" | event_name="ai.runtime.activity" | body_user_id=~"$user")[$__interval]))

defaults.noValue: No Plane C tactics in range

panels.title: Tactics by responsible agent
panels.description: The same observations grouped by the agent the lineage attributed them to, which is what turns "something read a credential" into "this agent read a credential".

targets.expr: sum by (body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_agent) (count_over_time(({service_name="defenseclaw"} | json | __error__="" | host_name=~"$host" | event_name="ai.runtime.activity" | body_user_id=~"$user")[$__interval]))

defaults.noValue: No Plane C tactics in range

panels.title: Agent activity — one record per tactic
panels.description: Each record carries the MITRE ATT&CK technique and the chain stage. The sequence is the finding: reading a credential is a lead, and reading a credential then minting an identity then uploading to a paste site is an incident.

targets.expr: {service_name="defenseclaw"} | json | __error__="" | host_name=~"$host" | event_name="ai.runtime.activity" | body_user_id=~"$user"

defaults.noValue: No Plane C tactics in range

panels.title: Kernel controls (Linux) — what DefenseClaw's kernel controls did
Hosts with enforcing controls
panels.description: Hosts whose `controls` policy was loaded in, or switched to, enforce mode in the range. Enforcement needs `enterprise.tetragon.mode: enforce`, an `enforce_ack` that matches the control-set digest, and a finished per-user burn-in; everything else runs in monitor mode and only counts.

targets.expr: count(sum by (host_name) (count_over_time(({service_name="defenseclaw"} | json | __error__="" | host_name=~"$host" | event_name="ai.runtime.kernel_policy" | body_user_id=~"$user" | body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_family="controls" | body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_mode="enforce")[$__range]))) or vector(0)

panels.title: Kernel denials
panels.description: Accesses a DefenseClaw kernel control refused with EPERM (`enforcement.block.applied`, initiator `kernel`). An in-place write to a shell rc file or user autostart unit, or a read of an ssh private key, by an enrolled agent's process tree.

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time(({service_name="defenseclaw"} | json | __error__="" | host_name=~"$host" | event_name="enforcement.block.applied" | body_user_id=~"$user" | body_defenseclaw_enforcement_initiator="kernel" | connector=~"$connector")[$__range])) or vector(0)

panels.title: Would-block (monitor)
panels.description: Accesses a kernel control in monitor mode would have denied, every user's, from the helper's own counter (plane_health would_block_delta). The series beside it shows the ones the gateway attributed to an agent.

targets.expr: sum(sum_over_time(({service_name="defenseclaw"} | json | __error__="" | host_name=~"$host" | event_name="ai.runtime.plane_health" | body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_plane="c" | unwrap body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_would_block_delta | __error__="")[$__range])) or vector(0)

panels.title: Agent activity with no hook decision
panels.description: Host-plane activity on a managed host that no hook decision covered: an agent's own shell escape, a detached job, an MCP server. The join only labels; it never blocks.

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time(({service_name="defenseclaw"} | json | __error__="" | host_name=~"$host" | event_name="ai.runtime.activity" | body_user_id=~"$user" | body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_hook_seen="false")[$__range])) or vector(0)

panels.title: Paused hosts and operator overrides
panels.description: Break-glass pauses (`enterprise linux tetragon pause`) and policies an operator moved to monitor or deleted. Both persist across helper and Tetragon restarts until the intent changes.

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time(({service_name="defenseclaw"} | json | __error__="" | host_name=~"$host" | event_name="ai.runtime.kernel_policy" | body_user_id=~"$user" | body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_event=~"paused|operator_override")[$__range])) or vector(0)

panels.title: Reconcile failures and orphans
panels.description: The sensor helper could not bring Tetragon to the policies it wants, or found DefenseClaw policies loaded that it no longer intends. Policies stay in or move to monitor; they never widen.

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time(({service_name="defenseclaw"} | json | __error__="" | host_name=~"$host" | event_name="ai.runtime.kernel_policy" | body_user_id=~"$user" | body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_event=~"reconcile_failed|orphaned")[$__range])) or vector(0)

panels.title: Kernel denials by control and connector
panels.description: Denials over time, split by the control that refused the access and the connector whose agent made it.

targets.expr: sum by (control, connector) (count_over_time(({service_name="defenseclaw"} | json | __error__="" | host_name=~"$host" | event_name="enforcement.block.applied" | body_user_id=~"$user" | body_defenseclaw_enforcement_initiator="kernel" | connector=~"$connector" | label_format control="{{.body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_control}}")[$__interval]))

panels.title: Would-block in monitor mode, by control
panels.description: What the controls would have denied while running in monitor mode (observe mode, and users still in burn-in).

targets.expr: sum by (control) (count_over_time(({service_name="defenseclaw"} | json | __error__="" | host_name=~"$host" | event_name="ai.runtime.activity" | body_user_id=~"$user" | body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_outcome="would_block" | label_format control="{{.body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_control}}")[$__interval]))

panels.title: DefenseClaw kernel policies
panels.description: State changes of the policies the sensor helper loaded into the host's Tetragon, by name, family, mode and state, with how many times each happened in the range. The log below has the timeline.

targets.expr: sum by (host_name, policy, family, mode, state, event) (count_over_time(({service_name="defenseclaw"} | json | __error__="" | host_name=~"$host" | event_name="ai.runtime.kernel_policy" | body_user_id=~"$user" | body_defenseclaw_policy_id!="" | label_format policy="{{.body_defenseclaw_policy_id}}", family="{{.body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_family}}", mode="{{.body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_mode}}", state="{{.body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_state}}", event="{{.body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_event}}")[$__range]))

defaults.noValue: No kernel policy changes in range

panels.title: Burn-in progress per user
panels.description: The latest burn-in progress of each user on each host (uid_progress every six hours, and uid_burnin and uid_ready when the state changes): covered agent hours with the event stream lossless, out of the hours burn_in needs. A would-block hit restarts the count. Covered time is agent use, not wall-clock time: 168h is about five to six working weeks for a full-time user.

targets.expr: max by (host_name, user) (last_over_time(({service_name="defenseclaw"} | json | __error__="" | host_name=~"$host" | event_name="ai.runtime.kernel_policy" | body_user_id=~"$user" | body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_event=~"uid_progress|uid_burnin|uid_ready" | label_format user="{{.body_user_id}}" | unwrap body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_covered_hours | __error__="")[$__range]))

max by (host_name, user) (last_over_time(({service_name="defenseclaw"} | json | __error__="" | host_name=~"$host" | event_name="ai.runtime.kernel_policy" | body_user_id=~"$user" | body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_event=~"uid_progress|uid_burnin|uid_ready" | label_format user="{{.body_user_id}}" | unwrap body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_needed_hours | __error__="")[$__range]))

panels.title: Kernel policy changes
panels.description: One record per state change of the sensor helper's reconciler (loaded, mode changed, removed, paused, operator override, ack stale, uid ready, Tetragon restarted, fallback). Never one per kernel event.

targets.expr: {service_name="defenseclaw"} | json | __error__="" | host_name=~"$host" | event_name="ai.runtime.kernel_policy" | body_user_id=~"$user"

defaults.noValue: No kernel policy changes in range

panels.title: Kernel denials
panels.description: Each denial carries the Tetragon policy name, the control-set digest, the guardrail rule it mirrors (`PATH-SSH-KEY`, `persistence.shell_profile_write`) and the user. The path and the command line are not exported.

targets.expr: {service_name="defenseclaw"} | json | __error__="" | host_name=~"$host" | event_name="enforcement.block.applied" | body_user_id=~"$user" | body_defenseclaw_enforcement_initiator="kernel" | connector=~"$connector"

panels.title: Your Tetragon policies: events from AI agents
Agent events
panels.description: Events of your own Tetragon policies (kprobe and LSM) whose process runs below an AI agent, in range (log.ai.runtime.kernel_event, repeats folded into a count). DefenseClaw reads these events and never adds, changes or deletes your policies.

targets.expr: sum(sum_over_time(({service_name="defenseclaw"} | json | __error__="" | host_name=~"$host" | event_name="ai.runtime.kernel_event" | body_user_id=~"$user" | unwrap body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_count | __error__="")[$__range])) or vector(0)

panels.title: Blocked by your policies
panels.description: Calls of an AI agent's processes your own Tetragon policies denied (override, sigkill or notify_enforcer in enforce mode). Alert DefenseClawCustomerPolicyBlocksAgents.

targets.expr: sum(sum_over_time(({service_name="defenseclaw"} | json | __error__="" | host_name=~"$host" | event_name="ai.runtime.kernel_event" | body_user_id=~"$user" | body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_outcome="blocked" | unwrap body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_count | __error__="")[$__range])) or vector(0)

panels.title: Would-block in monitor mode
panels.description: Calls of an AI agent's processes a denying action of your own policy matched while the policy ran in monitor mode.

targets.expr: sum(sum_over_time(({service_name="defenseclaw"} | json | __error__="" | host_name=~"$host" | event_name="ai.runtime.kernel_event" | body_user_id=~"$user" | body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_outcome="would_block" | unwrap body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_count | __error__="")[$__range])) or vector(0)

panels.title: Events your policies saw (every process)
panels.description: Every event of your own policies the sensor helper received in range (plane_health customer_events_delta), below an AI agent or not. Only the agent ones become records; the rest is counted.

targets.expr: sum(sum_over_time(({service_name="defenseclaw"} | json | __error__="" | host_name=~"$host" | event_name="ai.runtime.plane_health" | body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_plane="c" | unwrap body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_customer_events_delta | __error__="")[$__range])) or vector(0)

panels.title: Agent events by policy
panels.description: Events of your own Tetragon policies below an AI agent, by policy.

targets.expr: sum by (policy) (sum_over_time(({service_name="defenseclaw"} | json | __error__="" | host_name=~"$host" | event_name="ai.runtime.kernel_event" | body_user_id=~"$user" | label_format policy="{{.body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_policy_name}}" | unwrap body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_count | __error__="")[$__auto]))

panels.title: Policy, agent, action, outcome and hook join
panels.description: Which of your policies matched which agent's processes, what the policy did (action and outcome), and how the tool call was joined to a managed hook decision (exact, temporal, or none: no decision covered it).

targets.expr: sum by (policy, agent, action, outcome, hook_join) (sum_over_time(({service_name="defenseclaw"} | json | __error__="" | host_name=~"$host" | event_name="ai.runtime.kernel_event" | body_user_id=~"$user" | label_format policy="{{.body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_policy_name}}", agent="{{.body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_agent}}", action="{{.body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_action}}", outcome="{{.body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_outcome}}", hook_join="{{.body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_hook_join}}" | unwrap body_defenseclaw_ai_runtime_kernel_count | __error__="")[$__range]))

panels.title: Events of your Tetragon policies from AI agents
panels.description: One record per event (or folded repeats) of your own policy below an AI agent: the policy, hook, action, mode and outcome, the target (a content field: each destination's redaction profile decides whether it leaves the host), the agent, the user and the hook decision.

targets.expr: {service_name="defenseclaw"} | json | __error__="" | host_name=~"$host" | event_name="ai.runtime.kernel_event" | body_user_id=~"$user"
